messages:
alex.j: Heads-up — customer 'AcmeRetail' reported intermittent 429s during a heavy ingest this morning. They claim their project quota shows ~20M tokens remaining, but responses cite org-scoped limits. Requests are using a project-scoped API key and originate from a shared NAT IP. Anyone seen this exact interplay before? :thinking:

mira.p: can you paste a sample request/response (headers + body) and a request id? :mag:

alex.j: req id: req_01F2ABCDEF. Response body: \"{\"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\"}\". Response headers included `x-rate-limit-scope: org` and `x-retry-after: 12`. Logged ~12% of the calls returning 429s, others succeed.

jamal: quick context — our current attribution heuristic checks: 1) explicit API key scopes, 2) project quota, 3) IP/NAT heuristics, then falls back to org. But NATed IPs that show cross-project spikes can be elevated to org-burst attribution which can preempt project allowances.

alex.j: repro steps I used locally to reproduce (from a VM on same cloud egress range):
1) curl with their project API key from a GCP NATed IP (same /24 used by 3 projects)
2) fire 10 concurrent /v1/generate requests for ~90s
3) ~30% of requests receive 429 with org scope header

code snippet:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-proj-xyz" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\ 
  -d '{"model":"rw-1-small","input":"test"}' \\ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

sre-oncall-bot: @alex.j created INC-2026-112 for investigation (priority: high). Please attach traces and uplink logs.

mira.p: can you share org id + key id + exact timestamps (UTC)? I'll pull the attribution logs and check the burst bucket history and whether any other keys on that NAT consumed the org burst. Also check if they have any per-key override (billing-protection) flags enabled.

alex.j: org: org_7682, key: sk-proj-xyz, nat ip: 34.120.55.101. Timestamps: 2026-03-17T09:05:12Z — 2026-03-17T09:12:30Z. Customer insists no key rotation.

tara-support: I've asked the customer for exact app-level concurrency and whether they share the same egress with other teams. Requested they pause non-critical traffic while we investigate.

jamal: likely root cause: other tenants using the same NAT exhausted the org burst bucket. Because our heuristic currently elevates NATed IP attribution to org when cross-client churn is detected, the API key's project allowance can be preempted. Mitigations:
- immediate: add temporary IP exception / allowlist for sk-proj-xyz (ops-only) or bump org_7682 burst quota
- medium: add heuristics to prefer explicit API key/project quotas when a valid key is presented (prefer key scope > ip scope)

mira.p: I'll confirm with logs. If we confirm misattribution, propose config change to prefer explicit key scoping when project quotas exist, and create a migration plan to avoid sudden regressions. Also will add a fallback logging flag to better expose attribution decisions in responses.

billing-bot: noted. If ops requests an immediate org burst increase for org_7682, please include delta and duration. We'll estimate cost impact and pre-approve emergency short windows.

alex.j: thanks — collecting token counts and expected delta now. tagging @jamal for the temporary allowlist steps. We'll update customer within 30m. :thumbsup:
